title: The Sister Who Saw Visions During the Service
dates: In Tertullian's day, under the emperors Severus and Caracalla
datesNote: On the Soul gives no year: the sister is "now amongst us" as Tertullian writes. Jerome says Tertullian flourished chiefly in the reigns of Severus and Antoninus Caracalla.
placeNote: The passage names no city. Jerome says Tertullian was from Carthage, in the province of Africa.
shortDescription: In Tertullian's church, he writes, a woman sees visions during the Sunday service and speaks with angels, and at times with the Lord. After the people have gone, she reports what she saw, and every word is carefully examined to test whether it is true.

text: Tertullian, defending the New Prophecy against the charge of disorder, described how it actually worked in his own congregation. ‘We have now amongst us a sister whose lot it has been to be favoured with sundry gifts of revelation, which she experiences in the Spirit by ecstatic vision amidst the sacred rites of the Lord’s day in the church.’ She converses with angels, sometimes with the Lord; she sees and hears ‘mysterious communications’; she reads hearts and prescribes remedies for those who ask. What Tertullian wants his readers to notice is the discipline around it. She does not interrupt. ‘After the people are dismissed at the conclusion of the sacred services, she is in the regular habit of reporting to us whatever things she may have seen in vision, for all her communications are examined with the most scrupulous care, in order that their truth may be probed.’ On the day in question she had seen a soul in bodily form — ‘tender and lucid and of the colour of air’ — which is why Tertullian cites her in a treatise on the soul. It is one of the very few descriptions of a Montanist gathering from a participant rather than an enemy, and it does not look like the frenzy the opponents described: a woman with a recognized gift, a congregation that valued it, and elders who tested every word before receiving it.

whoTellsIt: Tertullian tells it, in his book On the Soul. The sister is "now amongst us" as he writes, and she reports "to us": he writes from inside her church, at the time.
He tells it to prove a point about the soul: that it has a body, which he says revelation confirms as well as reason.

He wrote as a follower of the New Prophecy. In the same book he speaks of "the true system of prophecy, which has arisen in this present age". Jerome, writing later, says Tertullian "lapsed to the doctrine of Montanus, and mentions the new prophecy in many of his books."
No one else records the sister, and Tertullian does not name her.

legacyAndToday: Nothing held yet: no later old writer in the Library has been found who keeps or quotes this passage.
uncertain: Tertullian is a sympathetic contemporary and an eyewitness, but a partisan. The woman is unnamed and no one else records her.
Whether every New Prophecy congregation examined visions this carefully cannot be known.
When. On the Soul gives no year. Jerome says Tertullian flourished chiefly in the reigns of Severus and Caracalla.
Where. The passage names no city. Carthage rests on Jerome's word that Tertullian came from there.
Who examined her words. Tertullian says she reported "to us", and does not say who "us" were.
